title: Pulseboard component lattice & token clarity playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Create a single, reusable console component (Pulseboard) that unifies cost sparklines, allocation chips, and a lightweight rollout signal-lane. The goal is to reduce visual drift across cost dashboards and rollout pages by prescribing tokens, spacing lattice, and permitted interaction variants. Scope: design system patterns (3 density variants), Figma library pages, token map + migration notes, accessibility checklist, and handoff assets for engineering. Deliverables: 1) Figma component set (Pulseboard master + density variants), 2) token spec sheet (names, intended aliases, fallback logic), 3) UX guidelines doc for when to use Pulseboard vs existing CostCard, 4) lightweight interaction prototype (hover/expand/mini-rollout), 5) accessibility and performance review notes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Figma masters added to design system library and linked in the Console DS file; 2) Token spec reviewed and approved by Tokens owner; 3) Engineering accepts the component implementation plan with max 3 nested DOM nodes for perf; 4) Accessibility checklist passes contrast and keyboard focus tests; 5) PM confirms Pulseboard covers 90% of observed cost+rollout use-cases in the product sample set.
comments: 2025-08-03 Maya Chen: Kickoff — scoped component surface after audit of 18 dashboard variants. Decided to combine cost mini-sparkline, allocation chips, and a 'signal-lane' to show rollout health at a glance.

2025-08-06 Liam O'Neill: Initial prototypes uploaded to Figma. Three density variants created: spacious, standard, compact. Added token candidates (pulse-gap-12, pulse-gap-8, signal-accent-500, cost-chip-elev-2).

2025-08-09 Design critique: PM Sasha requested clearer separation of rollout signals when canary traffic > 20%. Trade-off: stronger visual weight vs preserving token consistency. Proposal to use a bounded accent bar instead of full-surface color to reduce perceived contrast.

2025-08-11 Accessibility review by Iris K.: Contrast issues with signal-accent-300 on compact variant; recommend accent-500 or add 8% overlay. Also keyboard focus needed for chips and signal segments. Action: update tokens and provide focus ring token.

2025-08-13 Engineering sync with ENG-4022: Perf constraint — each Pulseboard instance must avoid heavy SVG path recalculation; prefer CSS-based sparklines with precomputed path data when possible. Decided to limit animated microstates to hover only, not continuous animation.
2025-08-15 PM review (Alex): Confirmed Pulseboard aligns with Console cost-explorer goals. Requested a short guidance section for when to fallback to CostCard (rich detail) vs Pulseboard (overview).
2025-08-18 Liam O'Neill: Updated Figma links and token table after accessibility changes. Preparing Handoff package and documenting migration steps for existing CostCard usage.
2025-08-19 Maya Chen: Submitted for design-review + DS owner approval. Included a Loom walkthrough and demo dataset for QA team.
decision: Adopt Pulseboard as the default compact overview widget for cost+rollout lanes. Standardize on three density tokens only (compact, standard, spacious). Use color token signal-accent-500 for primary rollout state, and add focus-ring token pulse-focus-2 for keyboard navigability.
next_steps: 1) Finalize token names and alias table; 2) Create token migration script (tokens owner + eng infra); 3) Handoff PR with Storybook examples and perf notes; 4) QA runs accessibility checklist against live implementation; 5) Add Pulseboard usage guidelines to Console component library page.
status_history: 2025-08-19 In Review: handed off to DS owner and engineering
